key.name: monitors
key.description: The monitors whose brightness should be adjusted.

key.name: builtin-monitor
key.description: The name of the built-in monitor.

key.name: clone-mouse
key.description: When enabled, the mouse cursor follows the brightness setting. When disabled, the mouse cursor always remains at full brightness. Controlling mouse cursor brightness can sometimes show the wrong cursor and introduce cursor lag, and may prevent the display from sleeping (the software cursor loop keeps the screen active). Disable it if you encounter cursor issues or if your computer stops sleeping. Note that when other Gnome Shell components clone the mouse (like the Zoom accessibility feature), this feature may not work correctly, or there may be multiple cursors shown on the screen.

key.name: brightness-up
key.description: Keyboard shortcut to increase the brightness by one step. Set to an empty list to disable.

key.name: brightness-down
key.description: Keyboard shortcut to decrease the brightness by one step. Set to an empty list to disable.

key.name: shortcut-step-software
key.summary: Keyboard shortcut step for software dimming.
key.description: How far each brightness shortcut press moves within the software dimming zone, as a fraction of that zone. The default 0.05 moves 5% of the software dimming range.

key.name: shortcut-step-hardware
key.summary: Keyboard shortcut step for hardware brightness.
key.description: How far each brightness shortcut press moves within the hardware brightness zone, as a fraction of that zone. The default 0.05 moves 5% of the hardware brightness range.

key.name: ddc-enabled
key.description: Control external desktop monitor brightness and contrast via DDC/CI.

key.name: software-dim-ratio
key.description: Portion of the slider allocated to software dimming when hardware brightness is at 0.

key.name: sync-monitors
key.description: Synchronize brightness and contrast across all monitors.
